en: The First Assembly on the Expedient Means for Offering and the Extensive Recitation Ritual of the *Mahāvairocanābhisambodhi-vikurvita-adhiṣṭhāna-sūtra*, Entering the Lotus Womb Matrix Ocean Assembly, the Maṇḍala Born of Compassion.
I prostrate to the Buddha Vairocana, whose pure eyes bloom like blue lotuses;
relying upon the King of Sutras, the Mahāvairocanābhisambodhi, I shall explain the various ritual procedures for making offerings.
To establish the sequential method of mantras, so that one may attain swift accomplishment therein,
and furthermore to cause the fundamental mind to be free from defilement, I shall now briefly proclaim it according to its essentials.
If one wishes to enter siddhi in this very life, one should contemplate according to what is appropriate;
having personally received the vidyā-dharma from the Venerable One, one should observe the corresponding signs and bring about accomplishment.
First, prostrate to the Guru who bestows empowerment and transmits the teachings; request the mantra and the practice to be cultivated.
Once the wise one has received the teacher’s permission, they should proceed according to a location suitable for the specific ground.
Amidst the peaks and ridges of Mount Miaoshan, within various grottoes between the two mountains,
there were once the dwellings where the noble disciples of the Tathāgatas roamed and resided in the past—
monasteries, stupas, hermitages, and the chambers of ancient seers. One should choose a place that accords with the inclinations of one’s own mind.
Out of compassion for sentient beings, he painted the great maṇḍala; next, he restored the Tathāgata’s opening of the Dharma-eye.
Able to deliver immeasurable multitudes of humans and devas, he is truly a supreme son born of the Tathāgata.
Possessing the power of pure wisdom, he is capable of endurance; with diligence, he seeks nothing of the worldly realm.
The transgressions born of negligence during this night, I now diligently purify and repent of them all;
with mind and eyes clearly and truly observing, I prostrate myself, casting my five limbs upon the ground.
I take refuge in the Perfectly Awakened Ones of the ten directions, Who possess the three bodies throughout the three times;
I take refuge in all the Mahāyāna teachings, And in the assembly of those who do not regress from bodhicitta;
I take refuge in the true words of the vidyās, And in all the secret mudrās.
With pure actions of body, speech, and mind, I reverently and immeasurably pay homage.
The mantra for the method of paying homage is as follows; employ the Seal of Holding the Ground:
"By this true word of paying homage, One is able to pay homage universally to the Buddhas of the ten directions."
Kneeling with the right knee on the ground and joining my palms, I contemplate and confess my past karmic offenses.
Accumulated through ignorance, I have committed various sins by means of body, speech, and mind;
because greed, hatred, and delusion obscured my heart, [I failed to honor] the Buddha, the True Dharma, and the Noble Sangha.
Toward my parents, my two teachers, and spiritual friends, as well as toward immeasurable sentient beings throughout the beginningless cycle of birth and death,
I have committed extremely grave and inexhaustible sins; now,
in the presence of the Buddhas of the ten directions who dwell in the present, I confess them all and vow never to commit them again.
The general mantra for the method of expiating transgressions is as follows:

Homage to the Buddhas of the ten directions and three periods of time, To the treasury of the True Dharma of the three types of eternal bodies, And to the assembly of great-minded beings with supreme vows and bodhicitta; I now take refuge in all of them with perfect sincerity.
The general mantra for the expedient means of taking refuge is as follows:
I purify this body, free from all defilements, along with those of the three times—body, speech, and mind.
Exceeding the number of atoms in oceans and lands, I offer them to all the Tathāgatas.
The mantra for the skillful means of offering the body is as follows: The form of the body is identical to a single-pronged vajra:

"Precious jewel of the pure bodhicitta and supreme vow, I now arouse [this resolve] to rescue all sentient beings— those bodies entangled by the accumulation of birth-suffering and the like, and those bodies harmed by ignorance."
To rescue, gather, and provide refuge so that they may be liberated, one should always benefit all sentient beings.
The mantra for generating the bodhicitta and forming the mudrā is as follows:
Within the infinite worlds of the ten directions, To the ocean-like assembly of all the Samyaksaṃbuddhas,
Through the power of various skillful means, and all the meritorious deeds performed by the sons of the Buddha for the sake of sentient beings— I now rejoice in them all without exception.
The Mantra of Rejoicing in Expedient Means:
With palms joined in homage, I now entreat all Tathāgatas, those Greatly Awakened Ones who save the world:
I pray that throughout the realms of the ten directions, you will constantly let fall the rain of Dharma from great clouds.
The Mantra of the Expedient Means of Exhortation says:
May ordinary beings, in their dwelling places, Swiftly cast off this body accumulated from manifold sufferings,
And attain the stainless state, Abiding securely in the body of the pure Dharma-realm.
The Mantra of Expedient Means for Invoking the Dharmakāya:
All virtuous karmic deeds that I have cultivated, For the sake of benefiting all sentient beings,
I now dedicate them all perfectly, To eliminate the suffering of birth and death and reach Bodhi.
The Mantra for the Skillful Means of Dedication says:
Furthermore, performing all remaining meritorious deeds, Such as reciting scriptures, walking meditation, and sitting in tranquility,
To bring about universal purity of body and mind, Out of compassion, one rescues and gathers both oneself and others.
The nature of the mind is thus free from all defilements; the body sits at ease as appropriate.
Clearly and attentively contemplate the first letter-gateway: a white, empty circle surrounded by ninefold rims.
One should know this as the form of the secret seal, as taught by all the Perfectly Enlightened Ones.
Joining the hands of Samādhi and Prajñā, raise both the wheels of emptiness and touch all the limbs; reciting the words of truth,
one enters the Buddha-samaya— the Samaya-mantra.
As soon as this secret seal is bound, one can purify the stage of the Tathāgata;
with the perfection of the stages (bhūmi-pāramitā) fulfilled, one accomplishes the path of the three dharma-realms.
As for the remaining secret seals, they shall be set forth in the following chapter on seals.
Next, bind the mudrā of the Arising of the Dharmadhātu, the emblem of secret wisdom.
Because it purifies body, speech, and mind, rotate it throughout the parts of the body.
With the hands of Prajñā and Samādhi, form both vajra-fists.
The two emptinesses rest upon his palm; the wind-banner is perfectly upright.
This is called the Dharma-realm, the secret seal of purity.
The mantra for the arising of the Dharma-realm:
Just as the intrinsic nature of the dharma-realm, one should contemplate one's own body;
or by means of words of truth, proclaim it three times.
One shall then see that which abides in the essence of phenomena, stainless like space.
Through the power of mantras and mudrās, and because they empower the practitioner,
in order to make that [realization] firm, one should visualize oneself as Vajradhara and bind the Vajrajñāna-mudrā:
the hands of śamatha and vipaśyanā are turned back-to-back.
The wheels of earth, water, fire, and wind support one another on the left and right;
the two voids rotate respectively and are joined within the palm of wisdom.
This is called the Wheel Dharma Seal, the most supreme and auspicious mudrā.
Before long, this person shall become equal to the Savior of the World;
through the power of mantras and mudrās, the accomplished one shall behold [the Buddha],
whose palms revolve like precious wheels as he turns the Great Wheel of Dharma.
Vajrasattva said: Having recited this mantra,
one should abide in meditative equipoise and clearly contemplate this body of mine as being Vajradhara himself.
Countless hosts of celestial Māras—whosoever beholds them, they shall be like Vajrasattva; do not give rise to a mind of doubt.
Next, don the vajra armor; one should contemplate the garment thus worn.
Flames of light arise from his entire body; because he uses these to adorn his person,
all Māras who act as obstacles, as well as other beings of evil intent,
scatter in all directions upon seeing him.
The two wind-wheels of śamatha and vipaśyanā support the fire-wheel above;
the two voids stand side by side within the palm.
Having recited that mantra, one should contemplate the stainless syllable.
The Vidyā of the Vajra Armor:
The syllable RA is brilliant white, adorned with a bindu;
like a luminous jewel in a topknot, it is placed upon the crown of the head.
Even the multitude of karmic stains accumulated throughout a hundred eons shall be entirely extinguished by this,
and both merit and wisdom will be brought to full perfection.
The mantra is as follows:
The mantra is identical to the Dharma-realm; immeasurable multitudes of sins are eliminated.
Before long, one shall achieve accomplishment and abide on the stage of non-retrogression.
In all places defiled by contact, one should apply this gateway of syllables.
Red in color and endowed with majestic radiance, Enveloped on all sides by a wreath of flames.
Next, for the sake of subduing Māra And restraining all great obstructors,
One should contemplate the Great Protector, The Vidyā that none can endure.
The mudrā is as explained below; the mantra of the Great Protector (*mahārakṣā*) is as follows:
"By the mere act of recollecting it, all the vināyakas, the rākṣasas of hideous form, and so forth—all of them shall flee and disperse."
Visualize before you the syllable RA, adorned extensively with the bindu;
it is a garland of pure radiant flames, brilliant as the glow of the morning sun.
By recollecting its sound and true meaning, one is able to eliminate all obscurations.
Liberated from the defilements of the three poisons, all phenomena are likewise so.
First purify the ground of one's own mind, then purify the ground of the path;
completely eliminating all faults and afflictions, their characteristic is like empty space.
Just as that which is sustained by the vajra, so too is this ground.
The yogin contemplates it with discernment; the five wheels are most profound and secret.
First, at the lower level, one should contemplate that wind-wheel.
The syllable *Ha* is established there, radiating black light and flames.
That mantra is as follows:
Next, above that, one places the water-mudrā (*vāruṇa-cakra*), its color like snow or milk.
The syllable Vā is established there, like crystal, the moon, or lightning.
The mantra for this is as follows:
Furthermore, upon the water mandala, one should visualize a vajra wheel.
Visualize the primordial syllable placed therein, with yellow light pervading the four directions.
That mantra is as follows:
This wheel is like a vajra; it is named Mahendra.
Flames of pure golden light flow forth everywhere.
Within that, one should contemplate the Teacher and the sons of the Buddhas;
in the water, one beholds white lotuses with exquisite colors and vajra stalks.
An eight-petaled lotus with filaments and anthers, naturally adorned with various jewels,
constantly emitting immeasurable light and surrounded by hundreds of thousands of other lotuses;
upon it, one should further visualize the lion throne of the Great Awakened One.
Adorned with precious jewels, within the great palace halls,
jeweled pillars stand in orderly rows; everywhere there are various banners and canopies,
interlaced with strings of pearls and the like, with exquisite jeweled robes hanging down and suspended.
Spreading clouds of incense and flowers, as well as clouds of various jewels,
they rain down diverse blossoms everywhere, scattering profusely to adorn the ground;
with harmonious and pleasing sounds, they perform all manner of music.
The palace is envisioned as pure and wondrous, with auspicious jars of *argha* water;
the king of jewel-trees is in full bloom, illuminated by lamps of *maṇi* gems.
Therein lie the grounds of samādhi and dhāraṇī, and the sovereign ladies-in-waiting.
The Buddha’s perfections and so forth, the wondrously adorned flowers of enlightenment,
skillful means as manifold performances, and the chanting of the sublime Dharma’s sounds—
by the power of my merit and the Tathāgata’s sustaining power.
And by the power of the *dharmadhātu*, one dwells making universal offerings.
The mantra of the consort Ākāśagarbha is as follows: [The Dharma should be recited many times; visualize according to the sūtra:
"By this, all is maintained; it is truly without difference."
The vajra-palms held in the void are the seal of empowerment (*adhiṣṭhāna-mudrā*);
all phenomena are unborn, for their intrinsic nature is fundamentally quiescent.
Contemplating this reality, place the letter A within it.
Next, one should transform the letter A into the Muni Mahāvairocana;
within his perfect halo, the multitudes of beings as numerous as the atoms of infinite lands appear everywhere,
with thousands of worlds serving as the measure of their number, as he emits wheels of blazing light.
Pervading the realms of sentient beings, he awakens them according to their dispositions;
his body and speech reach everywhere, and so too does his Buddha-mind.
With a pure golden hue like that of Jambudvīpa, he appears in this world for its sake.
Seated in the full lotus posture upon a lotus, absorbed in samādhi and free from all poisons,
his body draped in fine silken garments and naturally adorned with a topknot crown;
through the gateway of syllables he attains Buddhahood and likewise benefits all sentient beings.
Just as the Great Sun Tathāgata is contemplated by the yogin—
whether as one body or two bodies— so too do they enter into the fundamental essence,
and from it they likewise flow forth.
Proceed according to the previous method, invoking and employing the heart-mantras of the three families;
apply the wind-hook seal once more to invite them, so as to cause their hearts to rejoice.
Next, bind the perfume-seal, visualizing the palms facing outward and held upright.
Place the feathered end between the fingers of the right hand and visualize clouds of fragrant ointment,
their coolness pervading the entire world.
The mantra for fragrant ointment is as follows:
Next, the mudrā for offering flowers is explained: Interlace the eight fingers with the palms facing inward;
join the wrists and rest the tips of the *vāyu* (index) fingers against each other. The mudrā resembles the gesture of cupping flowers in one's hands.
The mantra is as follows:

Next, the dhāraṇī for burning incense is explained: extend the six [fingers] with the backs joined, raise them vertically, join the tips of the two *vāyu* [index fingers] at their sides, and let each *ākāśa* [thumb] rest against its respective *vāyu*.
The mantra is as follows:
Next, the mudrā of food and drink is explained: the two sides of the hands are joined together;
the tips of the fire, water, and wind [fingers] are united, while space rests beneath the wind, resembling the shape of a vessel for food;
with the wrists joined, it is presented forward.
The mantra is as follows:
Next is the mudrā of the Illuminating Lamp. Visualize the fist with the fire-wheel (middle fingers) extended upward;
the thumb rests upon the lower joint of the fire-finger. Contemplate the manifestation of infinite buddha-fields.
Before each and every Buddha, light performs the work of a Buddha.
The mantra is as follows:
Next, one should kneel with the palms joined in the universal gesture (*samantamukha-mudrā*), extolling the merit and wisdom of the Tathāgatas.
Having thus praised the assembly, numerous as the atoms of the world-system, one should utter pure sounds to seek *siddhi*,
chanting with earnest devotion three to seven times.
Next, recite verses of auspiciousness five, seven, or at least three times, awakening the deities and inspiring their joy.
The mantra is as follows:
Next, perform the offering of the argha mudrā: join the lotus [fingers] for śamatha and vipaśyanā;
open with the wind [finger] attached to the fire joint; let each space [finger] rest upon the wind [finger].
First the right knee, then the left, extending the mudrā to the forehead;
thus one pays homage three times to the Holy Deity.
With each offering, one should make a formal declaration, whereby one shall attain the Stainless Stage (vimalā-bhūmi).
The Samādhi of Freedom from Affliction and Coolness.
The Argha mantra is as follows:
Next, grasping the vajra, draw it back and cast it forth while shaking the golden bell.
Furthermore, perform the Turning of the Wheel of Dharma, and with clear visualization, grasp the Vajra.
Just as within the nature of the Dharmadhātu, one should abide in the Bodhicitta;
next, bind the seals of the directions and quarters, employing the Noble Acala.
Turning to the left accomplishes the expulsion;
turning to the right, as well as upward and downward, while fully touching the various parts of the body, makes the protective binding entirely firm.
As for the mudrā of the Mother of True Speech, it shall be distinguished below.
Once the solemn preparations are complete, one should display the fundamental mudrā;
placing it again upon the five locations, rotate it seven times or twice over.
Then, releasing the seal above the crown of the head while seated in half-lotus with body upright and mind focused, [one should recite:]
Alternatively, one may assume the *yogic posture*, positioned according to the directions as taught.
Standing directly in front of the body, one contemplates a single,
perfectly luminous image, pure and without blemish, like the orb of the full moon.
Within it is the form of the Honored One, With wondrous color transcending the three realms;
A garment of fine gauze adorns the body, And a jeweled crown holds down dark-blue locks of hair.
In the state of tranquil samādhi, His radiant blaze surpasses all lightning.
Just as within a clear mirror, the true countenance appears in its profound depth;
joy and anger manifest as forms and colors, and one's conduct and vows are equal.
With a body in accord with meditative absorption, the mind is clearly lucid and undisturbed.
The essence of the pure dharma is signless; through vows, one should deliver all sentient beings.
The milk-wind produces the four seals, and according to one [seal], accomplishment is achieved.
When the six months of practice are complete, one descends with light-footed supernormal powers.
Abiding in the Tathāgata-hook, arrange the syllables as clarified below; for those obstructed by the fire-born [demons], the mantra of Acala is as clarified in the middle fascicle.
The Ritual Manual for the Offerings of the Compendium of Mahāvairocana, Scroll One.
The Ritual Manual for the Maṇḍala of the Secret Seals and Emblems of the Various Honored Ones from the Mahābodhiketu Chapter of the Compendium of Mahāvairocana Sūtra, Scroll One.
2. At that time, Bhagavān Vairocana,
observing the great assembly, addressed Vajrapāṇi:
The Lord of Secrets, the Sattva, said:
"There is a dharma identical to Mahāvairocana, the adornment of the Tathāgata, the insignia of the Dharma-realm.
By means of this, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva adorns his body."
Abiding within birth and death, they traverse the various realms of existence.
In the assemblies of Tathāgatas throughout the dust-motes of lands,
they establish this Great Bodhi as the *ketu* (banner), the insignia of the Tathāgata.
The devas, nāgas, yakṣas, and the eight classes of beings pay homage from afar;
having received the teaching, they shall practice it accordingly.
Listen now with the utmost attention, and I shall expound it for you.
At that time, Bhagavān immediately abided in the samādhi of the power of harmlessness within his own body,
and proclaimed the unobstructed body of all Tathāgatas.
The light of the three peerless powers is the Vidyā-Queen;
thus it is said that the Vidyā-Queen is able to manifest as the Vajra-Guhyapati.
The ground of all Tathāgatas does not transcend the three dharmadhātus;
therein the bhūmis and pāramitās are perfected.
Forming the lotus-closure of the two emptinesses at the forehead, shoulders, heart, throat, and crown—
Seal five and recite the vidyā-queen.
This is the great seal of the Savior, the samaya of Perfect Awakening;
one abides within this seal.
Next is the Dharmadhātusaṃbhava-mudrā; one should abide in the syllable RAṂ, with the mudrā and mantra as previously described.
Next is the Dharmacakra-mudrā; clearly visualize Vajradhara, the wind-circle, and the seed-syllable of wind, with the mudrā and mantra as in the first assembly.
The practitioner of mantra, from these various samādhis,
immediately enters the syllable *Aṃ* and abides in the great bodhicitta.
Contemplating the body as a sattva, its color and form like blue crystal.
Abiding in the wheel of action (karmamudrā), one should universally form a wreath of flames.
Reciting the lower king of mantras, one should then construct the maṇḍala;
its measurement is two cubits from one's own elbow, for anything other than this is not auspicious.
Recite the verses for requesting the site as prescribed in the sūtras;
mark it with white sandalwood paste, universally offer fragrant flowers, and first perform the ritual of holding the site.
Only then may the Dharma-transmitting Ācārya proceed to take possession of it.
With five-colored threads, I prostrate to all Buddhas.
Mahāvairocana himself performs the empowerment;
Taking the eastern direction as the starting point, He holds the threads in correspondence.
Reaching the navel, it remains in space, gradually rotating to the right;
thus proceeding through the south and the west, it finally reaches the north.
The second establishment of the elements likewise begins from the initial direction.
Recalling all the Tathāgatas and their conduct as described above, one should circumambulate to the right,
then to the rear, and further around the victorious directions.
The Ācārya then turns back and takes his position in the nairṛti direction.
The recipient of the training, holding it fast, gradually proceeds toward the south;
from there, turning clockwise, he shifts his reliance to the direction of wind.
The master moves from his original position and takes up residence in the direction of fire.
The practitioner who upholds the mantra further cultivates this rite:
the disciple stands in the southwest while the master resides in the īśānī direction;
the student then circumambulates, shifting his position toward the southeast (the fire quarter).
The master moves from his original position and dwells in the direction of wind.
Thus the mantra-practitioner forms the signs of the four directions everywhere,
enters their midst in succession, and divides them into three positions.
Having already indicated the three stages, the characteristics of the ground are universally pervasive;
furthermore, each of these parts is further differentiated into three.
Among them, the first part concerns the path practiced in performing activities.
As for the remaining middle and latter sections, which are the abodes of the noble devas,
one should know their respective boundaries; with a sincere and reverent mind,
one should deploy the various noble deities.
Correctly manifesting the various marks, Evenly balanced and skillfully distinguished, The wondrous white lotus within the mind, The matrix perfectly symmetrical.
Within the matrix, all things are fashioned; The maṇḍala born of compassion.
Sixteen *aṅgulis* in measure, exceeding this is its extent;
the eight petals are perfectly full, with filaments and anthers all exquisitely adorned.
The seal of vajra-wisdom emerges everywhere from between the petals.
From within this lotus pedestal, the supreme venerable Vairocana appears;
golden in color and endowed with radiant splendor, his head bears a topknot crown.
He is the savior of the world with perfect light, free from all feverish affliction, abiding in samādhi.
The four wisdoms, the four practices, and so forth, are proclaimed within the eight secrets.
Above the Tathāgata Vairocana, his various samādhi retinues should be depicted to the east as the mudrās of universal omniscience.
Upon a three-pronged lotus, its color is entirely brilliant white;
a blaze of light encircles it on all sides, pure and pristine, pervading everywhere,
with its sharp peaks pointing downward.
By holding this, one subdues the four māras; therefore it is called the Seal of Omniscience.
It is able to possess manifold merits and give birth to the kings of all samādhis, and so forth.
Next, in the northern quarter, is the Mother of all Buddhas, the Guide;
resplendent with a true golden hue, she wears garments of white silk.
Her light shines everywhere like the sun, as she dwells in the meditative absorption of samādhi.
The mantra of the Buddha-mother Ākāśalocanā is as follows:
With the hands joined in the gesture of concentration and wisdom, the fingers of the wind-element (ring fingers) are tucked into the space between the thumbs and placed above;
its form is like a *khaṭvāṅga*. This is the seal of the Great Wisdom Sword (*mahāprajñā-khaḍga-mudrā*).
As taught by all Buddhas, this is able to sever all views,
namely the innate view of a self-body (*satkāyadṛṣṭi*).
The mantra says:
Samādhi and wisdom merge in an empty mind; the wind and space are coiled together,
its form like a conch shell and the like— this is called the Seal of the Auspicious Dharma Conch of Supreme Vows.
The Bodhisattvas, saviors of the world, all proclaim the stainless Dharma that leads to the ultimate peace of Nirvana.
The mantra says:
Samādhi and Prajñā joined and expanded, like the previous Khaṇḍa;
earth and space each supporting one another, wind and fire cause the heads to join.
This is the auspicious Lotus of Aspiration, [the seal] of all Buddhas, the Saviors of the World.
Without destroying the Vajra Seat, one awakens and is called a Buddha;
both Bodhi and the sons of the Buddha are all born from this.
The mantra says:
Forming fists with the two outer hands, extend the fire and wind fingers like hooks;
join the earth and space fingers upright, their shape like a *vajra*.
This is the Great Wisdom Seal of Vajra, which can destroy the city of ignorance.
One who awakens from sleep cannot be destroyed by gods or humans.
The mantra is as follows:
Forming fists within with concentration and wisdom, join the fire and space fingers, each held upright.
The wind-element is held within the fire; its form resembles a precious jewel.
This mudrā is the Mahāmudrā, known as the Tathāgata’s Crown.
As soon as it is bound, one becomes identical to the World-Honored One.
The mantra is as follows:
Form a fist with the hand of wisdom (*prajñā-hasta*), place the wind-finger (*anāmikā*) between the eyebrows;
this is called the "Concealed Heroic Mark" (*vīra-lakṣaṇa-garbha*). The Buddha shall always fulfill one's wishes.
By merely performing this, one immediately becomes superior among men.
The mantra is as follows:
Next, dwelling in the yoga seat, place the concentration and wisdom [mudrās] layered at the navel.
Just like the form of holding an alms bowl, this is called the Great Alms Bowl Seal of Śākyamuni.
The mantra is as follows:
With the previous mudrā, extend the hand of wisdom upward to bestow fearlessness;
it is able to grant fearlessness to all classes of sentient beings.
If one binds this great seal, it is called the Bestower of Fearlessness.
The mantra is as follows:
With concentration and wisdom as before, wisdom descends to bestow the boon;
such is the mudrā of granting boons, as taught by the Refuge of the World.
Those who have just now bound this seal, may all Buddhas fulfill their aspirations.
The mantra is as follows:
Extend the wind-wheel (the index finger) from the wisdom-fist, in the form of Bhṛkuṭī.
Abiding in the state of meditative equipoise, by means of this great mudrā,
the Buddhas, the saviors of the world, terrify all obstructors;
through the binding of this mudrā, one accomplishes siddhi according to one’s wish.
The hosts of great evil māras and all other obstructors will undoubtedly be driven away and scattered,
like a tuft of hair on the head placed between the eyebrows.
The mantra is as follows:
The fist of wisdom extends the water and fire; the wind and earth press down upon the wheel of space.
This is named the Eye of Compassion born from the World-Reliance of all Buddhas.
Visualize it placed within the field of vision; the wise one thereby attains the Buddha-eye.
The mantra for this, used to open the eyes at the time of consecration, is as follows:
Form fists within with the hands of meditative concentration and wisdom; extend the wind-fingers (index fingers) and join the tips of the thumbs.
This is the seal of the Supreme Vow Lasso (*praṇidhāna-pāśa-mudrā*), which destroys all who commit evil deeds.
The mantra practitioner binds it, thereby able to fetter all that is unwholesome.
The mantra says:
Forming a fist by joining samādhi and prajñā, the wind of prajñā is bent like a hook.
This is called the Hook Seal (*ākarṣaṇamudrā*).
It summons all those who dwell on the ten stages (*daśabhūmi*),
those possessed of the great mind of awakening (*bodhicitta*), as well as sentient beings of evil intent.
All who are summoned shall assemble.
The mantra is as follows:
With the previous mudrā, extend the fire finger and bend it; the fire and wind fingers are both like hooks.
This is called the Tathāgata-mind.
The mantra says:
With the previous fist, withdraw fire and wind; extend water to the navel of the Tathāgata.
Then, the aforementioned wind, fire, and water disperse from the Tathāgata’s waist;
the two mudrās each hold the vidyā-mantras.
Those two mantras are as follows:
With the waist or the fists bound within, extend and join the two water-fingers (anāmikā).

through the union of the wind and fire wheels,
the syllable *hara* transcends all afflictions.
Furthermore, one should perform recitation for one month; this is called the sixth month.
The celestial hosts, such as Śakra and Brahmā, will dwell afar and pay respectful homage, providing protection for all.
The gods and humans, medicinal herbs, and spirits; the vidyādharas and various rishis—attending and serving according to his commands;
the rākṣasas and the seven mother goddesses—all those who create obstacles—seeing the light of this place, flee and scatter like a fierce flame.
They revere him and stay far from evil;
having attained mastery over all things, they subdue those who are difficult to tame,
like the Great Vajradhara, benefiting all living beings.
Equal to Avalokiteśvara,
may all wishes be fulfilled; may you always, out of compassion,
protect both yourself and others.
Holding the jewel, one makes the great aspiration; with empowerment, one presents the five offerings.
With pleasing and wondrous verses, one thrice offers the argha water.
Through the methods of releasing the boundary and liberation, one extensively performs the initial expedient means.
Visualize the return to Caṇḍāla, and thereafter dwell in a secluded and tranquil place;
enter samādhi according to the instructions, constantly contemplating the sūtras, imprinting the sand,
and reflecting on the six recollections, up to the number of ten million.
Finally, the Buddha emits light; the practitioner’s karmic obscurations are exhausted, and they become identical to the Venerable Universal Illuminator.
The mantra of the empowerment phrase:
“Once the empowerment has been made firm, how does the ācārya possess the practice of great reality?
Having understood this vast meaning, [one realizes] the great merit of perfect awakening.”
He is called an ācārya;
even when no Buddhas appear in the world, such a person is named a Buddha.
All the wheels of syllables, if they reside within his limbs—
One should know that the syllable *HŪṂ*, the vajra-word, abides between the eyebrows;
the syllable *SA* is located below the chest, and this is called the lotus-word.
The syllable *A* is the primary life-force, and the syllable *VA* is named water.
The syllable RA is named Fire; the syllable HŪṂ is named Wrathful;
the syllable KHA is identical to Space, which is the so-called Point of Ultimate Emptiness.
One who knows this as the most authentic reality is called an Ācārya.
Having understood what the Buddha has taught, one should practice the deathless state;
one should contemplate the primordial syllable, adorned with a pure white bindu.
This is the most excellent hundred-fold heart-mantra: that all phenomena are fundamentally unarisen.
Observing with equanimity in the center, one can destroy the palace of ignorance.
Such is the Dharma taught by all the World-Honored Ones who have attained perfect enlightenment;
O Son of the Buddha, listen with a single mind as I arrange the gates of the letters.
The letter Ka is located below the throat; the letter Kha is above the uvula;
the letter Ga constitutes the neck; the letter Ca is in the throat;
the letter Cha is the root of the tongue; the letter Ja is in the middle of the tongue.
The syllable JA is the tip of the tongue; the syllable JHA is the root of the tongue;
the syllable ṬA is the shank; one should know that the syllable ṬHA is the thigh;
the syllable ṆA is said to be the waist; and the syllable TA is for the seated posture.
The final portion of the letter *ta* should be known as the feet; the letter *tha* as the belly;
the letter *na* as the two hands; the letter *dha* as the sides;
the letter *pa* as the back; and the letter *pha* as the chest.
The syllable MA is the two elbows; the syllable VA is beneath the arms;
the syllable MAṂ resides at the heart; the syllable YA is the mark of the secret organ;
the syllable RA constitutes the eyes; and the syllable LA is the broad forehead.
*E* and *i* are the two corners of the eyes; *u* and *ū* are the two lips;
*e* and *ai* are the two ears; *o* and *au* are the two cheeks;
the syllable *aṃ* is the word for *bodhi*; the syllable *aḥ* is *parinirvāṇa*.
Knowing all these phenomena, the practitioner attains perfect enlightenment;
the wealth of omniscience is ever present within them.
World-renowned as "Omniscient One," this is called *sā prajñā*.
At that time, the Buddha Vairocana addressed the Vajradhara Lord of Mysteries, saying:
"O Great Virtuous One, Vajrapāṇi!

This dharma is the most supreme secret of the Tathāgata’s secret seal; it should not be bestowed upon others indiscriminately, except for those who have already received empowerment, whose lineage is gentle and compliant, who are diligent and steadfast, who have made sublime vows, who revere their teachers and elders, and who are mindful of repaying their kindness."
Those who seek the Dharma by purifying both internally and externally, even at the cost of their own lives, are the true marks of my disciples.

Whether they be householders or renunciants, their lineage shall be preeminent; their complexions will be bluish-white or pure white, with broad heads, long necks, and foreheads that are wide and level. Their noses will be prominent, and their faces will be full, dignified, and well-proportioned. Such sons of the Buddha should be taught with diligent care.
If one acts otherwise than this, one violates the samaya.
The remainder is as explained in the original teaching.
May all sentient beings universally aspire to be born together within the Lotus Treasury World.

The *Compendium of the Great Ritual for the Extensive Recitation of the Lotus Womb Ocean Assembly Maṇḍala Born of Compassion*, derived from the *Mahāvairocanābhisambodhi-sūtra*, Volume Three. This single work in three volumes was requested and brought back by the three masters Jikaku, Chishō, and Shūei; however, its original text is not without variations.
As for this present edition that has been carved and printed, it is based on the original text of Great Master Jikaku.
Because successive transcriptions have introduced numerous errors, it has been collated and verified against the root sūtra and the *Vistara-vidhi*.
There were points that remained undecided which I have nonetheless ventured to annotate, awaiting future sages.

Alternatively, to prevent those who might treat the Dharma with contempt, I have occasionally corrected instances of disordered or omitted text by adding marginal dots based on my own teacher’s tradition.
This is also for the purpose of ensuring that the Dharma-treasure remains long in the world.
